name: Toggletip
description: A small info button that shows a short explanation when pressed and hides it again on a second press, Escape or a click elsewhere. Use it instead of a Tooltip when the button exists only to reveal the explanation, or where hover isn't available.
summary: Click-opened bubble with a short explanation
researchNote: A tooltip opened by click. Keeping the name because it behaves differently for assistive tech

elements.name: Trigger
elements.description: Button, often an "i" or "?" icon, with an accessible name such as "More info"

elements.name: Bubble
elements.description: Holds the explanation: plain text, no links or controls

elements.name: Arrow
elements.description: Points from the bubble to the trigger

variants.caption: Icon with text — visible trigger label

usageNotes: Use a Toggletip when the explanation should appear on a press. Use a Tooltip for a short label shown on hover and focus, and a Popover when the content includes links or controls.
Make the trigger a <button> with an accessible name. Put the message in a live region such as role="status" so screen readers announce it when it appears.
Close it on Escape, on a second press of the trigger and on a click outside, and leave focus on the trigger.
Keep the content to a sentence or two. Anything people need to complete a task belongs on the page, not behind an icon.
Give the trigger a target of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size, Minimum).
htmlOutline: Short explanation.
